status_summary: No reporting or White House document describing regular Office of Cabinet Affairs meetings of Deputy Secretaries, or an expanded agenda-tracking role for the office, was found as of 2026-10-09. A 2025-01-24 White House announcement staffed the Office of Cabinet Affairs and placed it, with Communications and Public Liaison, under Deputy Chief of Staff Taylor Budowich, who was also designated Cabinet Secretary. Axios reported on 2025-09-24 that he would leave at the end of September 2025; no successor as Cabinet Secretary was confirmed from the sources reviewed.

title: Have Cabinet Affairs run regular Deputy Secretary meetings and expand agenda tracking
uncertainties: Internal White House meetings are rarely reported, so absence of evidence is weak: Deputy Secretary meetings or agenda tracking may exist without public record. The finding rests on the researcher's three web searches, two further searches by the reviewer and the two sources cited. The President's Management Council, a different body, was not treated as a match. A later Cabinet Secretary seen only on a Wikipedia officeholder page was not used as evidence. The 2025-09-24 departure report was moved from the timeline to the summary because it is not a step toward or away from the recommendation. Absence check of 2026-10-16: one web search for a deputies process run by Cabinet Affairs in 2025 to 2026 returned only general Cabinet meeting coverage and transition-guide material, no description of regular Deputy Secretary meetings or an agenda-tracking function. Internal practice would rarely be public, so absence remains weak evidence.
